record_verbatim.plan_basis: Derived from the work the corpus' existing records imply: a hazard analysis and safety goal that exist, four functional safety requirements with four hardware and three software requirements beneath them, a system-level chain that had no system requirements until this authoring pass, and no post-development work at all. The plan is sized for the gap between that state and a coherent lifecycle, not for a greenfield programme.

progress_records.narrative: Two weeks behind on the hazard analysis. The cause is not technical: the safety manager who was to review the severity and controllability reasoning was unavailable for eleven days and there is no second person qualified to do it. The plan named a single point of failure and the risk register's RSK-002 predicted exactly this.

Supporting process definition is the package actually behind. It was given 20 days of float and has consumed 55. The float was real: the package had no predecessor and was therefore expected to finish early. The variance is absorbed, not recovered, and this is stated rather than hidden in a re-baselined date.

Still behind after the reviewer returned. Recorded as behind rather than complete because the functional safety concept was baselined with two unresolved contradictions against the safety goal's timing budget, and a concept cannot be baselined while its own arithmetic does not close.

Stakeholder needs and system requirements on plan. The package recovered because WBS-006 finished late and released the system engineer, which is the opposite of what the float was for. Recorded because it is the kind of dependency that a plan which treats packages independently would miss.

Verification is the package driving the forecast. Not because the measures are hard to write but because none of the nine new measures can be executed: there is no security harness, no injection node and no vehicle. The plan assumed the harnesses would be built by the verification package and it does not fund them. This is a planning omission and the risk register's RSK-004 names it.

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/<profile>/<id>.json, then record the approval as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block on the record, plus approval_ledger_ref naming one appended line in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. Do NOT add a revision_history entry: see docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Since the same day (amendment APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1) the approval is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl and the record keeps only a reference to it, so recording your signature neither bumps the revision nor invalidates any review digest.
